FILING_DESTINATION.detail: Fails on the 991c route (obligation:track-pathway:OK:ok_991c_deferred:deferred-sentence-court-record-expungement-under-991-c). The registry, specification and census name 'The Oklahoma district court that entered the deferred sentence'. The FILING_DESTINATION row for that set and the PDF caption parenthetical say the same. But the required-before-filing item for the 991c petition caption (production-field-map ok_991c_deferred-primary-filing-2.court_identity; participant-instructions.md line 316) tells the participant to write 'the Oklahoma district court for the county where the arrest information is located', with the field map's reason 'the committed track registry records the venue as the district court in the county where the arrest information is located'. That is the section 18 venue, not this track's, so the packet names two different courts for this motion and says the registry recorded the wrong one. The 991c proposed-order caption copies the petition's. The 991c caption also says 'see the filing instructions in this packet' and step 1 says to read 'the filing instructions page for your route', but the 991c set has no such page. The other 7 sets name their registry destination correctly.

FEE_AND_WAIVER.detail: Fails on the 991c route, on the waiver limb. The 7 section-18-style sets pass: no held source sets the district court filing fee (the OK compiled profile has no feeRules and no court-fee figure; the OSBI $150 arrest-record fee is stated, sourced), and each fee-disclosure page names 'the district court clerk in the county where you file' for the fee and for whether a fee-waiver route exists. The 991c set has no fee-disclosure page. Its only fee text is the instructions row 'Fee as recorded: Not established for the section 991c motion ... Fee waiver as recorded: Not established.' The fee itself is reachable only through generic step 5 ('ask that office what it charges'); for the waiver, no authority is named anywhere for this route. The registry holds no 991c fee or waiver, so a named authority is the deliverable, and it is missing.

SERVICE.detail: Fails on the 991c route. The 7 other sets state a named mechanism from the registry: service 'By the court's notice', with the court giving 30 days' notice to the prosecuting agency, the arresting agency, OSBI and any agency holding records. For 991c the packet's only service text is 'Service as recorded: Not established. Notice as recorded: Not established for this motion.' It gives no rule, no nobody-is-served statement and no authority to ask. The registry holds none (rules.service 'Not established'), and its 991c buildBlockers record the text of 22 O.S. 991c, including whether notice is required, as unread, so a named checkable authority (the district court that entered the deferred sentence, or its clerk) is the most the packet can honestly give. It gives nothing.
